answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by pricing identity as a decaying bond. A newcomer locks a crystal of spendable stake that stays frozen across several epochs; cheap clones then pay a rising real cost. At the dawn of each epoch the protocol re-prices that bond against recent registration volume, so a sudden flood becomes self-defeating. A relic of prior attested work and sealed grades discounts the bond, rewarding continuity rather than mass-cloned accounts.
